ECE 6390 / Antennas and arrays

Arrays

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how element pattern and element arrangement jointly determine radiation.

For identical similarly oriented elements in the stated uncoupled model, the total field is Eelement times AF. A uniform linear array has AF = Σₙ exp[jn(kd cos θ + β)] for n = 0 to N − 1, where θ is measured from the array axis.

The array factor describes coherent addition of fields. A normalized power |AF/N|² describes relative angular shape; absolute directivity requires integration of the complete element-times-array intensity over solid angle.

General arrays may use complex weights with varied magnitudes. A prescribed equal-amplitude array keeps every installed feed magnitude the same and varies allowed phases or locations instead. Pattern multiplication here assumes mutual coupling is neglected.

Example

Two equal in-phase contributions give AF = 2 and squared magnitude 4 relative to one contribution. Dividing by N² makes that coherent peak 1 and removes its absolute scale.

    Practice

    1. Can an array-factor maximum fill an exact common axial null of the identical element pattern in this model?

    Use the product Etotal = Eelement AF.

    The common element null remains zero because it multiplies the array factor. A direction that an element cannot radiate in this ideal model remains a null of the product.
